title: A garment bankruptcy fraud case set aside $30,000 for San Francisco

beats.text: Three San Francisco garment factories left workers waiting for wages.

visual.sub: Workers waited more than a year before the state issued checks

beats.text: A state fund paid more than $865,000 from industry fees.

visual.label: Workers waited more than a year before the state issued checks

beats.text: In 2008, a state civil appeal rejected personal liability for the companies’ wages.

beats.text: The federal bankruptcy case traced separate pools of seized money.

visual.kicker: Seized assets moved into a different distribution process

beats.text: An April order covered about $1.46 million across two actions.

beats.text: Its 45 allocations add up to just over $1.32 million.

beats.text: The schedule assigned $30,000 to San Francisco’s Tax Collector.
The court also set aside $100,000 for California’s Employment Development Department.
